conclusion: Logical kernarg alignment is a wire-visible kernel ABI contract, while page alignment is private allocator backing. CP25 can therefore accept logical alignment 8, retain owner-session-fixed 4096/65536 backing, and return 8 honestly. Existing v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D publishes bytes to the exact owner/allocation subrange; no KERNARG v2 opcode is needed or permitted.
decision: Store logical and backing alignment separately, validate that the daemon-issued VA satisfies the requested logical alignment, keep backing alignment out of the ACK, and bind v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D to the same owner and allocation generation before SUBMIT_AQL. Preserve page_size_lifetime=owner-session-fixed until a later checkpoint deliberately changes and tests it.
invalidated_assumptions: A public logical alignment must equal the allocator's page-backed alignment.
Accepting alignment 8 requires either abandoning page backing or reporting 4096 in the wire ACK.
Generic kernarg publication needs a new payload-v2 KERNARG opcode instead of the existing v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D carrier.
observation: The fresh two-generation live probe allocates 512 bytes with logical alignment 8 over hidden 4096-byte backing, publishes the complete 280-byte kernarg manifest at offset 64 through v1 MEMORY_COPY_H2D, and completes SUBMIT and UNMAP with owner and generation checks. The response retains logical alignment 8 and never exposes backing alignment as the ABI value.
question_or_symptom: How can the daemon accept the runtime's ordinary alignment 8 while preserving honest page-backed allocation and the existing memory carrier?
